may_be_looking_for: People diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (lupus).
People who have a partner willing to join the study and participate together.
may_exclude_people_who: Are unable to read and write in English for the study questionnaires.
Are considered by their rheumatologist as unable to participate (for example, due to cognitive problems or severe illness).
patient_summary: This completed study explored how communication, social support, and confidence in managing lupus affect health over time. Researchers assigned 150 people with lupus and their partners to receive either counseling focused on problem-solving and support, or an informational film about lupus. Participants were followed for 12 months to track physical and mental health, disease activity, and coping.
patient_title: A Study on Counseling and Education for Lupus Patients and Their Partners
questions_to_ask_clinician: Whether my partner is willing to participate with me.
Whether I can read and write English well enough for the study tasks.
Whether I have any cognitive or severe health issues that might make participation difficult.
source_grounding: This description is based on public clinical trial registry data and may not include all study details. Consult the study team or your doctor for complete information.
uncertainty_notes: This study has been completed and is no longer enrolling participants. Results may not yet be publicly available or may not apply to all individuals. The information here does not recommend which approach is better.
what_researchers_are_studying: Researchers wanted to understand how communication between patients and their partners, social support, and self-efficacy (belief in one's ability to manage lupus) relate to health in people with lupus over time. They also compared two approaches: one counseling-based and one educational film.
